issues.summary: No test for mixed per-environment lookup failure, and no test that the chain list is fetched once per environment
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.spec.ts mocks getNetworksByChainId (line 98) but never asserts its call count, and the only failure test (line 266) rejects for every environment. Fetching once per environment with per-environment isolation is the PR's main new behaviour (safes.v2.service.ts:214-233), so a regression there would go unnoticed.

issues.summary: The warn→debug change in getNetworkFromChainId only affects positions, not the overview
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The overview calls getChainIdToNetworkMapping through ZerionRepository (zerion.repository.ts:15), so the PR body's reason for the change doesn't hold. The only remaining caller is positions (zerion-positions-api.service.ts:222). Its _getChainName still warns 'not configured' when no name resolves, so little visibility is lost.

issues.summary: Chain-list lookup failure is logged as PortfolioRequestError
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.ts:225 reuses LogType.PortfolioRequestError for a /v1/chains failure, so it gets mixed in with real portfolio fetch errors (lines 314-329, and zerion-portfolio-api.service.ts:165). This is a small monitoring cost.

issues.summary: Chain-list lookup is on the critical path with no negative caching, so a Zerion outage adds a timeout to each overview request
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: When the cache is cold or the fetch fails, _fetchAndCacheMapping (zerion-chain-mapping.service.ts:160ff) runs on every request and only successes are cached. It is awaited at safes.v2.service.ts:74. Portfolio calls hit Zerion during an outage anyway, so the extra impact is limited latency.

issues.summary: Concurrent cold-cache requests don't share one in-flight chain-list fetch
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: getChainIdToNetworkMapping checks the cache and then fetches, with no in-flight dedupe (zerion-chain-mapping.service.ts:107-128). This existed before the PR; the overview now just calls it more often. The window is short and cached for the TTL.

issues.summary: The comment says validation happens before any Zerion call, but the chain-list lookup now runs first
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.ts:74 awaits resolveZerionChainNames, which may hit Zerion /v1/chains, before the comment and resolveSafes at lines 76-78. Portfolio calls are still gated on validated entries, so this is a documentation mismatch.

issues.summary: getChainIdToNetworkMapping is now public, but its doc still says '(for positions)'
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: zerion-chain-mapping.service.ts:104-107 still says '(for positions)' and sits among private helpers, while its real callers are now getNetworkFromChainId and ZerionRepository. The doc is stale.

issues.summary: The new repository only forwards to the datasource; schema parsing stays in the datasource and the repository has no test
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: zerion.repository.ts:12-18 just delegates. ZerionChainsSchema.parse happens in the datasource (zerion-chain-mapping.service.ts:169), which goes against the Raw<T>/repository-parse convention. The split existed before, but the new repository keeps it. The repository is thin, so the cost is minor.

issues.summary: The zerionChains test helper is a literal fixture rather than a builder
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The integration spec at lines 30-44 builds the chain list from fixed network names. These have to match specific Zerion network names and chain IDs, so randomising them with faker adds little. No zerion-chain builder exists to reuse.

issues.summary: The zerionChains helper is loosely typed instead of using ZerionChains
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: Line 33 returns { data: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }. Typing it would catch schema drift at compile time, but the payload is parsed by ZerionChainsSchema at runtime and the tests would fail then anyway.

issues.summary: A test name still says 'enabled chain'
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The test at safes.v2.service.spec.ts:303 is still named 'enabled chain'; the PR's wording is 'Zerion-listed'. This is only naming.

issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The method returns Record<chainId, network> (zerion.repository.interface.ts:8). A plural 'networks' for the whole map is a reasonable name, so this is naming preference.

issues.summary: Map<boolean, …> could be named mainnet/testnet locals
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.ts:214-218 works correctly, and the Set of isTestnet values usefully skips fetching an environment that isn't in the request. This is style only.

issues.summary: Docstrings on private helpers describe what they do rather than why
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The cited docstrings on resolveSafes and resolveChains (safes.v2.service.ts:138, 171) were not added by this PR. The PR only edited the resolveZerionChainNames and fetchPortfoliosOncePerIdentity docs, and those explain non-obvious behaviour (once per environment, fallback semantics).

issues.summary: Removing the per-chain PORTFOLIO_ENDPOINT gate widens the rollout to every chain Zerion lists
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: This is the stated intent of the PR: 'derives support from Zerion's own chain list, gated only by the global FF_ZERION_ENABLED kill switch'. The description names the kill switch as the only lever, so the claim that it was left unstated is incorrect.

issues.summary: Overview and positions now resolve Zerion chain names differently
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The PR description lists 'the positions endpoint still reads balancesProvider.chainName first' as a known follow-up. The overview dropped the config name on purpose, because a wrong config name caused the Robinhood bug. Falling back for chains Zerion doesn't list is correct, because the portfolio has no slot for them.
